step1_analysis.description: A diamond buffer-based line driver output stage. It features a complementary push-pull output (Q5, Q6) with current mirroring (Q7-Q10) to enhance output drive capability for ADSL line driving.

paper_reference.title: An ADSL-RT Full-Rate Analog Front End IC With Integrated Line Driver

voltage_gain.description: Midband voltage gain of the buffer

sky130_expected.calculation: As an emitter-follower based buffer, the gain is typically close to 1 V/V (0 dB). The 75 dB reported in the paper likely refers to the open-loop gain of the preceding op-amp or the dynamic range of the ADC.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Diamond buffers inherently have a closed-loop gain slightly less than unity due to VBE drops and finite transconductance.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by transistor fT and parasitic capacitances. Modern processes easily exceed 100 MHz for this topology.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The 1.1 MHz reported in the paper is the ADSL signal bandwidth requirement, not the maximum physical bandwidth of the circuit.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = VDD * I_total. With 1.8V supply and ~2mA quiescent current, P ~ 3.6mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Scaled down significantly due to the 1.8V supply compared to the 12V line driver supply used in the original paper.

output_power.description: Maximum signal power delivered to the load

sky130_expected.calculation: P_out = (V_peak^2) / (2 * R_load). For V_peak = 0.5V and R_load = 1k, P_out = 0.125 mW = -9 dBm.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Severely limited by the 1.8V supply voltage and load resistance, much lower than the 12V ADSL line driver.
Fixed by the prompt's requirement to use VDD=1.8V.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure voltage gain, bandwidth, power consumption, and output swing of the line driver.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Line Driver Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Parameters
.param R_val=1k

* DUT
R1 VSLD N1 {R_val}
R2 N4 GND {R_val}
Q1 N1 Vref1 N2 npn
Q2 N3 Vref2 N4 npn
Q3 GND IN N2 pnp
Q4 VSLD IN N3 npn
Q5 N5 N2 OUT npn
Q6 N6 N3 OUT pnp
Q7 N5 N5 VSLD pnp
Q8 OUT N5 VSLD pnp
Q9 N6 N6 GND npn
Q10 OUT N6 GND npn

* Generic BJT Models (since netlist uses BJTs)
.model npn npn (is=1e-14 bf=100 vaf=50)
.model pnp pnp (is=1e-14 bf=100 vaf=50)

* Sources
VSLD VSLD 0 1.8
VVREF1 Vref1 0 0.9
VVREF2 Vref2 0 0.9
VIN IN 0 DC 0.9 AC 1 SIN(0.9 0.1 1MEG 0 0)

* Load
RL OUT 0 1k

* Control Block
.control
  * DC Operating Point and Power
  op
  let power = -i(VSLD) * 1.8
  print power

  * AC Analysis for Gain and Bandwidth
  ac dec 100 1 1G
  let gain_db = vdb(OUT)
  meas ac midband_gain find gain_db at=10k
  meas ac bandwidth when gain_db=-3 fall=1

  * Transient Analysis for Output Swing
  tran 10n 5u
  meas tran v_max max v(OUT)
  meas tran v_min min v(OUT)
  
  quit
.endc
.end
